title: Microsoft Entra: Conditional Access for Entra ID account recovery
summary: The roadmap facts, recovery prerequisites, licensing and documented controls are supported. Remove the unsupported assurance that Conditional Access leaves the identity-verification data flow unchanged, and clarify the recovery settings path and beta API limitation.

claims.claim: Account recovery lets users regain organisational account access after losing all registered authentication methods.
claims.quote: enables users to regain access to their organizational accounts when they've lost access to all registered authentication methods.

claims.claim: The planned change enables Conditional Access policies to protect the recovery flow.
claims.quote: This feature adds additional support for protecting the account recovery flow by enabling CA policies to be applied.

claims.claim: The supplied roadmap status remains In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development"

claims.quote: Account onboarding and recovery (preview)

claims.quote: Use the Account onboarding and recovery user action to protect bootstrap separately from ordinary resource access.

claims.quote: Identity-verified onboarding and account recovery require identity verification regardless of whether a Conditional Access policy requires it.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; controls[1].note; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Terms of use is unsupported for the onboarding and recovery user action.
claims.quote: The following controls aren't supported for these journeys: Terms of use. Require authentication strength.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; controls[1].note; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Require authentication strength is unsupported for the onboarding and recovery user action.
claims.quote: The following controls aren't supported for these journeys: Terms of use. Require authentication strength.

claims.claim: Most other Microsoft Entra-specific controls are also unsupported for this action.
claims.quote: Most other Microsoft Entra-specific controls also aren't supported for this action.

claims.claim: Microsoft states no current plan or timeline to add support for those controls.
claims.quote: There's no current plan or timeline to add support for these controls.

claims.claim: The policy must explicitly configure Client apps as Browser and Mobile apps and desktop clients.
claims.quote: Under Conditions > Client apps, set Configure to Yes, explicitly select Browser and Mobile apps and desktop clients, and select Done.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: All resources policies apply to recovery unless the tenant-wide onboarding and recovery exclusion is enabled.
claims.quote: Without this exclusion, policies targeting All resources also apply to onboarding and account recovery events.

claims.claim: Policies directly targeting the user action still apply with the global exclusion enabled.
claims.quote: Enabling the exclusion removes the Account onboarding and recovery user action from All resources policies; policies that directly target the user action still apply.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Unsupported recovery requirements can block recovery or leave intended requirements unenforced.
claims.quote: Unsupported recovery policy requirements can block recovery or leave intended requirements unenforced.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; controls[0].note
claims.claim: Account recovery requires admin enablement and its policy is disabled by default for new and existing tenants.
claims.quote: In the new Account recovery policy experience, the policy is disabled by default for both new and existing tenants. Enable the policy before users can use account recovery.

claims.claim: Managing recovery settings requires Authentication Policy Administrator.
claims.quote: The Authentication Policy Administrator role to manage Account recovery settings.

claims.claim: Recovery enablement and TAP issuance settings are reached through Microsoft Entra admin center > Entra ID > Account recovery > Settings (preview).
claims.quote: Go to Entra ID > Account recovery. Open Settings (preview). Use Actions after recovery in Account recovery settings to choose how users register replacement methods.
claims.fix: Keep the shared path, which reaches the settings page, and append to the row note: 'On this page, enable the Account recovery policy; under Actions after recovery, choose Issue Temporary Access Pass.'

claims.claim: No automation operation for tenant recovery enablement or post-recovery TAP issuance is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph account recovery settings enable policy Temporary Access Pass issuance API. Opened recovery settings, recovery overview and FAQ; results document portal settings and individual TAP management, not these recovery settings.

claims.claim: The user action is reached through Entra ID > Conditional Access > Policies > New policy > Target resources > User actions > Account onboarding and recovery.
claims.quote: Under Target resources, select User actions, then select Account onboarding and recovery.

claims.claim: Graph documents no policy user-action value or operation for targeting Account onboarding and recovery.
claims.quote: Searched: conditionalAccessApplications includeUserActions account recovery onboarding Graph policy API urn. Opened beta conditionalAccessApplications; search also returned v1.0. Both list only urn:user:registersecurityinfo and urn:user:registerdevice.

claims.claim: The global exclusion is at Entra ID > Conditional Access > Settings (Preview) > Global exclusions > Account onboarding and recovery (Preview).
claims.quote: Browse to Entra ID > Conditional Access > Settings (Preview). Under Global exclusions, enable the Account onboarding and recovery (Preview) exclusion.

claims.claim: PATCH /beta/identity/conditionalAccess/settings updates the tenant-wide exclusion.
claims.quote: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/identity/conditionalAccess/settings

claims.claim: The request sets exclusions.allResourcesExclusions.userActionExclusions with userAction accountrecovery.
claims.quote: "exclusions": { "allResourcesExclusions": { "userActionExclusions": [ { "state": "enabled", "userAction": "accountrecovery" } ] } }

claims.claim: Updating userActionExclusions requires supplying the complete desired collection.
claims.quote: When updating userActionExclusions, supply the complete desired collection, not only the entries that changed.

claims.claim: The settings update requires Policy.ReadWrite.ConditionalAccess.
claims.quote: Delegated (work or school account) | Policy.ReadWrite.ConditionalAccess; Application | Policy.ReadWrite.ConditionalAccess

claims.claim: The settings operation is a beta API subject to change.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version in Microsoft Graph are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.
claims.fix: Append to the beta qualification: 'Microsoft does not support using beta APIs in production applications.'

claims.claim: Applied policy details are at Entra ID > Monitoring & health > Sign-in logs > sign-in > Conditional Access.
claims.quote: Browse to Entra ID > Monitoring & health > Sign-in logs. Select a sign-in item from the table to view the sign-in details pane. Select the Conditional Access tab.

claims.claim: GET /v1.0/auditLogs/signIns reads sign-in records and applied Conditional Access results.
claims.quote: GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/auditLogs/signIns?$filter=(createdDateTime ge 2024-11-01T14:13:32Z and createdDateTime le 2024-11-10T17:43:26Z) and conditionalAccessStatus eq 'failure'

claims.claim: Viewing applied Conditional Access results requires permissions to view both logs and policies.
claims.quote: To see applied Conditional Access policies in the logs, administrators must have permissions to view both the logs and the policies.

claims.claim: Recovery involves government-issued documents and biometric checks through third-party identity verification providers.
claims.quote: Identity verification involves processing government-issued documents and biometric data through third-party providers.

claims.claim: Microsoft advises reviewing privacy, retention and regional compliance requirements before deployment.
claims.quote: Review your organization's privacy, data retention, and regional compliance requirements before deploying account recovery.

claims.claim: Conditional Access does not change recovery's identity-verification data flow.
claims.quote: Searched: account recovery Conditional Access identity verification data flow biometric government documents unchanged. Opened recovery overview, recovery settings, FAQ and CA identity-verification guidance; none explicitly establishes an unchanged data flow.
claims.fix: Replace 'CA does not change that data flow; it adds conditions to the journey.' with 'CA adds conditions to the recovery journey.'

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Recovery is an existing user-driven flow for complete authentication lockout.
claims.quote: The user provides their account identifier at sign-in and indicates they can't access their account.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance controls
claims.claim: After successful validation, recovery issues a TAP by default.
claims.quote: Issue Temporary Access Pass on | Default for new and existing tenants. Successful account validation issues a TAP for the established registration flow.

claims.where: Governance controls; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The default TAP issuance setting does not itself enable tenant account recovery.
claims.quote: The default TAP issuance setting doesn't enable account recovery for your tenant.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Report-only mode does not evaluate user-action-scope policies.
claims.quote: Report-only mode excludes policies in the user-action scope from evaluation.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Microsoft advises an approved isolated enforcement pilot for action policies without report-only support.
claims.quote: Use an approved, isolated enforcement pilot for action policies when report-only isn't supported.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance; controls[3].governs
claims.claim: Conditional Access results in sign-in logs can identify a policy blocking recovery.
claims.quote: If recovery is blocked, review the Conditional Access results in the sign-in logs to identify the blocking policy.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The recovery FAQ requires Microsoft Entra ID P1 for account recovery.
claims.quote: Users need a Microsoft Entra ID P1 license to use account recovery.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Recovery also needs Face Check licensing through Entra Suite or standalone.
claims.quote: A Face Check license is also required, either through Entra Suite or standalone.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The identity verification provider has a separate cost determined by its Security Store offer.
claims.quote: If your scenario uses an identity verification provider, purchase the provider's services separately through the Microsoft Security Store. These services aren't included in the Microsoft Entra licenses listed in the table.

claims.claim: The licensing table includes Account recovery in P1, P2, ID Governance, Entra Suite and Microsoft 365 E7.
claims.quote: | Feature ** | Free | Microsoft Entra ID P1 | Microsoft Entra ID P2 | Microsoft Entra ID Governance | Microsoft Entra Suite | Microsoft 365 E7 |; | Account recovery |  | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |

claims.claim: Face Check is an add-on for Free, P1, P2 and ID Governance, and included in Entra Suite and Microsoft 365 E7.
claims.quote: | Feature ** | Free | Microsoft Entra ID P1 | Microsoft Entra ID P2 | Microsoft Entra ID Governance | Microsoft Entra Suite | Microsoft 365 E7 |; | Face Check | Add-on | Add-on | Add-on | Add-on | ✅ | ✅ |

claims.claim: Face Check pricing is based on unique Face Check verifications.
claims.quote: Face Check with Microsoft Entra Verified ID pricing is based on unique Face Check verifications performed by the verifying authority during the billing cycle.

claims.claim: Face Check can be enabled through Entra Suite or pay-as-you-go charged to a linked Azure subscription.
claims.quote: Enable as a Microsoft Entra Suite trial or paid subscriber. Face Check is included as a full capability in the Microsoft Entra Suite. Or enable in pay-as-you-go where your Azure subscription received charges per each individual Face Check verification performed from your tenant.

claims.claim: Face Check attempts returning a matching score or failed face matching emit billing events.
claims.quote: Verification request returns failed face matching: Processing the face matching between the biometric data and the credential data failed | Yes; Verification request returns a face matching score | Yes

claims.claim: Licensing is mixed, combining recovery entitlement with Face Check and separately purchased provider services.
claims.quote: Users need a Microsoft Entra ID P1 license to use account recovery. A Face Check license is also required, either through Entra Suite or standalone. The identity verification provider cost depends on the offer you subscribe to in the Microsoft Security Store.

claims.claim: The variable cost rating rests on Face Check pay-as-you-go billing per verification.
claims.quote: Or enable in pay-as-you-go where your Azure subscription received charges per each individual Face Check verification performed from your tenant.

claims.claim: The cited recovery FAQ and licensing pages state no numerical verification rate.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Entra account recovery Conditional Access account onboarding recovery settings API Graph default global exclusion licensing Face Check. Read the recovery FAQ, licensing table and Face Check billing page; none states a numerical verification rate.

claims.claim: Recovery profiles determine user scope through user groups.
claims.quote: Account recovery supports a phased rollout through identity verification profiles. Each profile targets specific user groups

claims.claim: Recovery does not support B2B, external guest or federated users.
claims.quote: Account recovery doesn't support B2B users, external guest users, or federated users.

claims.claim: Verified ID must be enabled as a recovery prerequisite.
claims.quote: Verified ID enabled and Face Check configured in your tenant.

claims.claim: Face Check must be configured as a recovery prerequisite.
claims.quote: Verified ID enabled and Face Check configured in your tenant.

claims.claim: Recovery requires an ID verification profile for recovery.
claims.quote: An ID verification profile for recovery, configured in Microsoft Entra Verified ID, and a dedicated test group.

claims.claim: Recovery requires Microsoft Authenticator meeting the versions listed in the setup page.
claims.quote: Microsoft Authenticator version 6.2610.7075 or later for Android, or version 6.8.58 or later for iOS, installed on users' devices.

claims.claim: Step-up and recovery are unsupported when initiated from a mobile app with Link to Windows as active broker.
claims.quote: Identity verification step-up and recovery aren't currently supported when initiated from a mobile app while Link to Windows is the active broker on the device.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans support in a later Link to Windows version.
claims.quote: Support for both features is planned in Link to Windows version 1.26111.xxx, starting November 30.

claims.claim: Tenants using recovery in the earlier preview must enable the new policy to continue.
claims.quote: If your tenant already uses account recovery from an earlier preview, you also need to enable the new policy to continue using the feature.

claims.claim: The Microsoft pilot guidance requires working emergency access accounts excluded from the pilot.
claims.quote: Working emergency access accounts excluded from the pilot, following Manage emergency access accounts.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends starting with a test group and recovery profile in Evaluation mode.
claims.quote: Create a profile in Evaluation mode targeting a small test group to validate the identity verification flow.

claims.claim: Microsoft advises testing replacement-method registration, not only identity verification.
claims.quote: Apply your settings and test recovery through registration of a replacement method, not just successful identity verification.

claims.claim: The global onboarding and recovery exclusion's default is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: Conditional Access global exclusions account onboarding recovery default enabled disabled. Read CA identity-verification guidance, Target resources and recovery settings; these explain enabling the exclusion and recording its previous state, not its default.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The checklist asks the reader to configure a recovery profile in Evaluation mode but the table has no profile control row.
claims.quote: start with a test group and an ID verification profile in Evaluation mode; table rows cover recovery settings, CA user-action policies, global exclusions and sign-in logs.
claims.fix: The At rollout step's ID verification profile mode and group-scope control has no corresponding table row. Remove 'and an ID verification profile in Evaluation mode' from that checklist step; do not add a row in this correction.

claims.claim: Recovery enablement, post-recovery TAP issuance and Conditional Access policy configuration are separate controls.
claims.quote: Enabling the policy is separate from configuring actions after recovery, such as issuing a TAP or removing stale credentials. Use Conditional Access to protect the Account onboarding and recovery user action.

claims.claim: Account recovery substitutes automated identity proofing for manual help-desk verification in total-lockout scenarios.
claims.quote: Account recovery uses automated identity proofing to reduce reliance on manual help desk verification.

claims.claim: All resources policies can prevent users from establishing or restoring credentials.
claims.quote: Without this exclusion, policies targeting All resources also apply to onboarding and account recovery events. Those policies can prevent users from establishing or restoring credentials.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: The global exclusion affects every All resources policy in the tenant, not just the pilot.
claims.quote: This setting affects all policies targeting All resources, not just the policy used in your pilot.

claims.claim: Microsoft advises recording the global exclusion's previous state for rollback.
claims.quote: Record the exclusion's previous state in your rollback plan.

claims.claim: Microsoft advises configuring and testing a user-action policy rather than treating the global exclusion as replacement protection.
claims.quote: Configure and test the intended user-action policy rather than treating the exclusion as a replacement for protecting onboarding and recovery.
